lesson_title: The Outside Angle Equals the Two Far Corners
hook_text: Stretch one side of a triangle out like a ramp. The angle you make outside equals two angles inside, and they are not the ones next to it.
clip_script: Take any triangle and stretch one side straight out past a corner, like a ramp. The angle between the ramp and the other side is the exterior angle. Here is the fact: it equals the two FAR corners added together, the two you did not stretch past. Far corners 50 and 60? Exterior angle 110. Far corners 35 and 85? Exterior angle 120. Why? The exterior angle and the near corner sit on a straight line, so they make 180. The two far corners and that same near corner make 180 too, because every triangle's corners add to a half-turn. Both are 180 take away the near corner, so they are equal. Two lines, proved. Use it: exterior angle 120, one far corner 45, the other is 75. The trap is grabbing the near corner. Say it with me: outside equals the two far corners.
visual_style: A triangle on a whiteboard with one side extending into a ramp; the exterior angle glows, then the two far corners glow and slide together to match it; a two-line proof writes itself and the near corner is struck through in red when grabbed by mistake.
pacing: Construction and two measurements fast, the two-line reason at speaking pace, one worked use, the rhythm line.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson for classifying triangles, the angle sum and the error museum.
